clauses.reason: Operative lead (the enacting words that introduce the order). It carries no command of its own beyond introducing Sec. 1 to 4, so it ends with them at the close of December 24, 1990, the only day the order covers.

Closes all executive departments and agencies for the last half of the scheduled workday on Christmas Eve, December 24, 1990 ("closed and their employees excused from duty for the last half of the" scheduled workday). Ends by its own terms at the close of that day, 1990-12-24. No exclusive-reading alternative arises because the order states a day, not an until-date.

Lets agency heads keep chosen offices and employees on duty for the full scheduled workday on December 24, 1990. The permission is usable only on that day, so it is exhausted by the day's end, 1990-12-24.

Treats Monday, December 24, 1990 as within EO 11582 and 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) for pay and leave. It names that one day, so it ends with the day, 1990-12-24; pay and leave already credited are accrued effects (see savings).

States that the order applies to Federal departments and agencies only and does not direct State or local governments. It limits the closing in Sec. 1 and has no operation after the closing, so it ends with it on 1990-12-24.

research_rationale:
EO 12739 of December 17, 1990 (Half-Day Closing of Government Departments and Agencies on Monday, December 24, 1990), read in full in the held Federal Register text (55 FR 52165, Federal Register of December 19, 1990; machine-extracted text layer, not a page image). Identity: number, date and subject in the printed heading agree with the census register row (1990-12-17, George H.W. Bush). The order closes executive departments and agencies for the last half of the scheduled workday on Christmas Eve, December 24, 1990, lets agency heads keep offices and employees at work that day for national security or other essential reasons, treats that Monday as within EO 11582 and the cited pay and leave statutes, and limits itself to Federal agencies. Legal reading: a one-day closing that ends by its own terms at the close of December 24, 1990. Inventory: the five dossier clauses (operative lead, Sec. 1 to 4) cover every operative sentence. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning. Machine hits for this order: current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 0. The packet's by-number scan of held order texts (LOOKUPS) was read for this order; the only held text citing this order is its own Federal Register text; the dossier chain holds no later event and the own-text scan found no wording signal.
